name: neko
why: A dynamically typed language with its own VM from the Haxe lineage, an unusual corner of language design worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Neko is a high-level, dynamically typed programming language with its own bytecode virtual machine. Its compiler turns a .neko source file into a bytecode .n file, which the VM then runs. It can also be embedded as a scripting language inside other applications, and its C foreign function interface lets it call C libraries. The homepage says the compiler can be used as a standalone command-line tool or as a library for compile-and-run in interactive languages.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Neko as a common runtime for several languages, so language designers can focus on language design while reusing a fast runtime and existing libraries for the filesystem, network, databases, and XML. It was developed as part of Motion-Twin's R&D effort for better languages.
brief.how_it_works: Source is compiled by the Neko compiler, which the homepage says is written in Neko itself, into bytecode in a .n file. The lightweight, optimized VM runs that bytecode and can be embedded in applications. Libraries are reached through the C foreign function interface, and other languages can have generators that target Neko.
brief.install_notes: The homepage shows no install steps. The Homebrew caveat supplied with the package says to add this line to your .bashrc or equivalent: export NEKOPATH="$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib/neko". This came from the package metadata, not from the homepage. The Homebrew package installs four executables: neko, nekoc, nekoml, and nekotools.
brief.standout: Neko positions itself as a shared runtime for multiple languages rather than a single language: other language designers can compile to its bytecode and reuse its VM and libraries. The homepage also includes a built-in example, saying mod_neko lets Neko generate web pages inside Apache and that the site itself is generated with Neko.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no version number, release date, or last-updated date. It does have a copyright line attributing it to the Haxe Foundation, and it says Neko is free software under the MIT License. I did not check a repository or release history.
brief.caveats: The homepage gives no version, platform list, or install instructions beyond the Homebrew note. Its scout note calls Neko part of the Haxe lineage, but the homepage does not say that outright; it only credits Motion-Twin and carries a Haxe Foundation copyright. The docs it links to (specifications, VM documentation, mod_neko introduction) were not fetched because the page gave no URLs for them.
quotes: Neko is a high-level dynamically typed programming language.
If you need to add a scripting language to your application, Neko provides the best tradeoff between simplicity, extensibility and speed.
The compiler is written in Neko itself, and is still very fast.
